speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension; can you tell me if you have been vomiting, and if so, is it forceful or projectile?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, Amylase_Lipase

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Intussusception and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information. Since intussusception was suspected but you noted no vomiting, could you describe the abdominal distension and whether the baby has passed stool or gas recently?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal Ultrasound demonstrates the classic "target sign" or "pseudokidney sign" in the right lower quadrant, consistent with intussusception. No free fluid or perforation is noted.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception

REQUEST IMAGES: Please confirm the ultrasound images showing the classic "target sign" in the right lower quadrant have been reviewed by the radiology team.

REQUEST TEST: None needed at this time; this case is urgent for reduction.
